title: XIN LIU Releases New Single ‘STRANGE’ Ahead of Forthcoming Album
summary: “STRANGE” first made its live debut on Aug. 1 during XIN LIU’s XANADU 2.0 Tour in Shenzhen.
body: On Aug. 5, XIN LIU released “STRANGE,” the first single from her forthcoming album. The track marks a new step in the Chinese singer, songwriter and producer’s evolving sound, pairing retro funk with live instrumentation and contemporary pop production. “STRANGE” first made its live debut on Aug. 1 during XIN LIU’s XANADU 2.0 Tour in Shenzhen, four days ahead of its official release. The performance offered audiences an early introduction to the track’s energetic groove and playful attitude. Following its live debut, anticipation for “STRANGE” continued to build ahead of its Aug. 5 release. After arriving on streaming platforms, the track quickly gained traction across digital music platforms, extending the momentum generated by its Shenzhen debut. Built around drums, guitar and bass, “STRANGE” draws on the rhythmic energy of funk while bringing the genre into a contemporary setting. Live instrumentation gives the track an organic, tactile quality, while modern production adds a sharper edge to its retro-inspired sound. The song centers on the idea of stepping outside a predetermined path. Once the expected trajectory changes, the world begins to look different — strange, unpredic…

title: Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone could take some inspiration from Android phones
summary: A leaked render of the 20th anniversary iPhone reveals a radical new redesign, with some familiar elements.
body: TL;DR Apple may be prepping radical design changes for the 20th anniversary iPhone, according to a new leak. The leaked renders show curved glass on the front and back with two horizontally placed cameras at the back. We’re also seeing what appears to be a hole-punch selfie camera on the screen, reminiscent of present-day Android phones. The iPhone is expected to see a radical shakeup this year, with Apple’s first-ever foldable likely to be revealed during the fall event next month. However, the company will reach a bigger milestone in 2027, marking 20 years since the first iPhone was revealed in 2007. A new leak is giving us our first potential look at the next-gen iPhone model Apple could introduce to celebrate. Leaker Yogesh Brar shares a couple of images on X that appear to show the 20th anniversary iPhone from multiple angles, including a clear view of its sides. It also appears to show a quad curved display on the front and a similarly curved glass on the rear panel. The images reveal dual rear cameras positioned horizontally, rather than vertically as on the iPhone 17. But for as interesting as all that is, it’s also hard to ignore some of the discrepancies in this particul…

title: Mariko Hayashi’s New Essay Collection Rises to No. 1 on Billboard Japan Book Hot 100
summary: Izumi Tsubaki's Gekkan Shoujo Nozaki-kun Vol. 18 follows at No. 2.
body: Mariko Hayashi’s 80-dai ni Naru to Taitei Bokeru ka Shinu. 70-dai wa Kamisama kara Ataerareta Tokubetsuna Jikan hits No. 1 on the Billboard Japan Book Hot 100 released Aug. 20. The essay collection — whose title roughly means “most people in their 80s end up with dementia or dead. your 70s are a special gift from god” — was released in May. The veteran writer, now 72 years old, speaks candidly on health, fashion, work, money, personal connections and hobbies. A string of television appearances this week drove the title to lead brick-and-mortar while collecting points across all five metrics including e-commerce (EC), e-books, subscriptions and social media. The title claims the top spot in its 11th chart week and marks the first time a shinsho (a compact nonfiction paperback format) title has topped the chart. Izumi Tsubaki’s Gekkan Shoujo Nozaki-kun Vol. 18 follows at No. 2, placing No. 2 in both brick-and-mortar and EC. Keigo Higashino’s 2023 novel Anata ga Dareka wo Koroshita enters at No. 3 following the release of its paperback edition. Higashino, who passed away at age 68 on July 23, places two other titles in the top 20 this week: Eien no Kioku at No. 6 an…

title: ESPN’s streaming plans are getting more expensive: Here’s what you’ll pay
summary: Bundles including Disney Plus and Hulu are also affected.
body: TL;DR ESPN streaming plans and bundles are increasing in price. Plans are increasing by $1 to $3 per month. Adjustments also affect many streaming bundles that include ESPN. Last week, we learned that Verizon will soon increase the prices for its Disney Plus, ESPN, and Hulu perks , with plan add-ons increasing by a buck or two per month starting in September. Now, ESPN has announced that its streaming subscriptions and the bundles they’re included in will be going up in price for everyone, not just Verizon subscribers. As we’ve learned from 9to5Mac , ESPN has announced price hikes for its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited streaming plans. Select is increasing from $13 to $14 per month (or $140 per year, up from $130), while Unlimited is jumping from $30 to $32 per month (or $320 per year, from $300). Bundles including ESPN along with Disney Plus and Hulu are going up, too.

Referrals only count when a new Edge Mobile user installs through your link and searches with Edge on two different days within 14 days. Microsoft really wants you to try out its Edge browser — and it’s willing to put its money where its mouth is. The tech giant has previously awarded Edge usage over competing browsers with monetary incentives, and it is now paying users for convincing others to make the switch.

title: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s
summary: A select few hits have led the chart for at least 10 weeks.
body: Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement. Olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. (Songs began logging longer No. 1 stays after the Hot 100 adopted electronically tracked data, according to Luminate, in late 1991.) In 2017, Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber, tied the No. 1 run of “One Sweet Day.” By 2019, Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, collected 19 weeks atop the Hot 100, a mark matched by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” beginning in July 2024 and — as of the Aug. 29, …

title: Yung Miami Is Ready for Her Solo Debut Thanks to ‘Spend Dat’: ‘People Are About to Eat Their Words’
summary: On the heels of the top 20 Billboard Hot 100 hit, the rapper's new album will arrive later this year.
body: As the first weeks of summer began to swelter, Yung Miami thought she had finally finished recording her long-awaited debut album. Then “Spend Dat” upended her plans. The infectious, pro-scammer anthem that she “always knew” would be a hit soundtracked the season, making its way from the New York Knicks’ locker room, where the song blared in a post-NBA Finals celebration captured on social media, to the Billboard charts, topping Rap Airplay for five weeks across July and August. Now, the MC from Opa-locka, Fla. — part of greater Miami — has her sights set on owning the fall, too. The rapper born Caresha Brownlee, 32, will soon unveil that as-yet-untitled solo album, nine years after she and JT first burst onto the scene as City Girls. Over the past two-and-a-half years, Yung Miami has locked in with a team of writers and producers — including J. White, Cheeze Beatz and Go Grizzly — curating “one big family” to help craft the album across recording sessions in Atlanta and Miami. “I’m finally in a safe spot, and the energy is great,” she says. “I’m ready.” Related Lucky Daye & Yung Miami to Headline Billboard’s R&B Hip-Hop Live 2026 Concert Doja Cat Appears Not to…

title: Galaxy Ultra power users should feel right at home on next year’s S27
summary: The S Pen will apparently still be on the left.
body: TL;DR Leaked renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra show the phone could come with an iPhone 17 Pro-style rear camera island. Additional renders imply other aspects of the phone’s external hardware will be largely unchanged from Galaxy S26 Ultra. The S27 Pro, S27+, and standard S27 will apparently see other, minor design tweaks. With Samsung’s new foldables and Google’s Pixel 11 series here, the next major release to look forward to in the US Android market is the Galaxy S27 series, which should debut in early 2027. This morning, we got a look at early leaked renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra , which show us that Samsung seems to be taking pretty direct design inspiration from Apple’s latest Pro iPhones. Now, we’re taking a look at yet more renders that show the phone from more angles. Superleaker Ice Universe has posted a handful of renders on X, showing that “Aside from the redesigned camera layout,” the upcoming S27 Ultra “will look nearly identical” to this year’s Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, with the same display size, left-hand S Pen placement, and more. The other S27 phones will apparently see some other minor layout changes, however.

title: YouTube is bringing lots more content types to 24/7 Stations feeds
summary: Tuning you in to some new ideas for Stations.
body: TL;DR YouTube introduced Stations earlier this year, featuring 24/7 content streams from musical artists. Now Google is expanding Stations to also include podcasts, creator content, and more. Access is only getting started with a small number of creators initially. Like any good streaming service, YouTube is always working to find the next big hook that will keep viewers glued to their screens, video after video. Earlier this year, we spotted a fresh addition to YouTube’s offerings in the form of Stations , 24/7 streams that appeared designed to connect you with an endless feed of content from your favorite musical artists. And now, Stations are getting a bit of an expansion. YouTube is constantly trying out new experiments, and this month, the service shares that its latest involves building Stations around even more diverse content than just music. While you’ll still see Stations from musical performers, they’re also starting to expand to cover podcasts, media channels, and just regular creator content.

title: Philips Hue is working on a more affordable TV sync box
summary: It's apparently a lot less expensive, but it won't do as much.
body: TL;DR A UK retailer has listed the unannounced Philips Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The new version offers only a single HDMI input, among other compromises. The Lite model is listed at retailer Very for £109.99 compared to the existing premium model’s £299.99. The Philips Hue Play HDMI sync box 8K lets you synchronize your smart lights with what’s happening on your TV to create a “fully immersive light syncing experience” (as Hue puts it), matching the color and brightness of your smart lights with your video content in real time. It’s cool, but it’s also wildly expensive at an MSRP of $385. Now, though, it looks like Philips Hue is set to release a new, stripped-back version at a more affordable price. As spotted by Hueblog , UK retailer Very has published a listing for an unannounced sync box from Philips, the Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The Lite version is shown as having one HDMI input (to the current model’s four), meaning you’ll be limited to syncing lights with a single device’s video. It’ll apparently be much less expensive, though: the Hue Play Sync Box Lite is listed at £109.99, about a third the price of the 8K model’s £299.99 UK MSRP.

title: YouTube’s latest UI change improves how you get to a video’s juicy bits
summary: The update adds a visual timeline indicator when double-tapping to skip.
body: TL;DR YouTube may be rolling out a new seek UI on Android that shows how much time you’ve skipped through a video. The change appears on the stable YouTube app, but it hasn’t reached every device. The new behavior could be part of a broader YouTube UI refresh. YouTube’s interface has become something of a moving target lately. The company was only recently testing a new button arrangement on Android that removed text labels from the controls under videos. And now, a small change to how YouTube shows skipped time appears to be rolling out to some Android users. The change involves YouTube’s familiar double-tap gesture for skipping. Currently, you can double-tap the right side of the screen to jump forward or the left side to rewind, while touching and holding the scrub bar lets you manually move through the video. In the current UI, double-tapping skips forward or backward without showing how much time you’ve moved. When manually scrubbing, however, YouTube displays the amount of time you’ve skipped in the video interface, as seen in the screenshot below.

title: Now Playing on Pixel may be getting its big missing feature back
summary: Google could bring back Now Playing notifications after breaking them with a recent update.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google updated the Now Playing app on Pixel earlier this year — and removed the option to show notifications. It may now be working to bring notifications back. Google also appears to be working to add support for multiple users, which isn’t supported yet. Now Playing remains one of the most compelling reasons to buy a Pixel still . In March this year, Google brought a major update to Now Playing, advancing it with its own dedicated app . But the update also brought a few feature cutbacks and challenges, such as removing notifications about tracks being played in your surroundings. This broke popular use cases for using Now Playing’s notifications to import songs into apps, such as Last.fm. What followed was dissatisfaction from users, which Google is now looking to address. It is working to add notifications for the currently playing track back to the app with a future update.

title: Buying the Pixel 11? Maybe consider this poll-winning alternative first
summary: This poll nearly offered up a huge upset, but a heavyweight won the bout in the end.
body: The Google Pixel 11 props up the company’s new flagship series and will be the popular choice to joining the premium Android ownership club. But, it’s by no means the only contender out there. If you’re torn about reaching for the Pixel 11, which alternatives should you consider? My colleague Brady Snyder offered up his five best options , and we asked readers to vote on their preferred candidate from this list. With over 4,200 votes in, we were just a handful of votes from a surprise upset.

title: With 4K/240fps slow-mo, this upcoming flagship could blow rivals out of the water
summary: vivo's upcoming X500 Pro could offer better slow-mo and wider dynamic range than any other phone on the market.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR vivo has started officially teasing the X500 series, featuring its upcoming camera-centric flagships. The vivo X500 Pro will use a custom Sony sensor that offers 17 stops of dynamic range, producing well-lit shadows even with bright highlights. The Pro is also claimed to be the first phone to capture slow-mo at 4K@240p. It’s been mere months since we took a good look at vivo’s colossal Ultra camera masquerading as a phone with one of the farthest-reaching zoom lenses . Come September, major phone giants will keep us busy with new releases. Among them, vivo is set to launch a new flagship camera phone with some serious upgrades previously unseen on phone cameras. In a recent Weibo post , vivo’s product manager Han Boxiao revealed camera upgrades coming for the upcoming vivo X500 series. Boxiao writes that while previous devices have aced at phone photography, the upcoming X500 series “aims to take mobile video to another level.” When I tested the X300 Pro from earlier this year, I found it to outpace the iPhone 17 Pro in video , and the upcoming phones could take a major leap, as the representative suggests.

title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

title: I want to love the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, but one silly change is stopping me
summary: To make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold roughly 1mm thinner, Google made this compromise.
body: Before the Pixel 11 Pro Fold became official, I shared a wishlist of changes I wanted Google to make for its next foldable. To my surprise, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold offers many of the upgrades I needed to take Google foldables seriously again. It’s thinner and lighter, has slimmer bezels and better screens, and supports faster 25W Qi2 wireless charging. However, Google also made an unexpected change to the Pixel 11 Pro Fold that I can’t overlook. To make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold about 1mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, compromises had to be made. The one you probably noticed is the smaller 4,806mAh battery capacity, but that isn’t the one I care about.

title: Google fixed this Google Maps issue on mobile, but it’s back now on Android Auto
summary: The traffic view works on phones but disappears behind the wheel.
body: TL;DR Traffic lines are disappearing from Google Maps on Android Auto for some users. The issue appears limited to Android Auto, not Maps on phones. Some users say the problem started after the Immersive Navigation update arrived. Google Maps users really can’t seem to catch a break lately. Not long after Google fixed a bug that made color-coded traffic lines disappear across Android, iOS, and desktop, the same issue has now appeared in Android Auto. Several users in the Android Auto community and on Reddit are reporting that Google Maps no longer shows the familiar green, yellow, orange, and red traffic lines on their car’s screen. The problem appears to be limited to Android Auto, with affected users reporting that traffic displays normally when they open Google Maps directly on their phones.

title: Pixel 11 owners can’t play Genshin Impact, but a fix is on the way
summary: Genshin Impact unplayable on your new Pixel 11 phone? You're not alone, but a fix is coming.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel 11 series owners are reporting that Genshin Impact is unplayable due to severe graphical problems. The developer reportedly said that PowerVR GPUs don’t meet its minimum requirements. Google has apparently confirmed the issue while noting that a fix will arrive in an upcoming game update. The Google Pixel 11 phones are powered by a Tensor G6 processor, which uses a PowerVR GPU. Unfortunately, you can’t play Genshin Impact on these new phones. Thankfully, a solution is in the works. Pixel 11 series owners reported severe graphical issues when trying to run Genshin Impact on their phones. These problems made the game unplayable as a result. The issue has also been flagged via Google’s Issue Tracker .

title: Crazy report reveals Exynos 2700 could outperform Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro
summary: Just FYI, Samsung reportedly conducted these tests itself.
body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly tested its Exynos 2700 chip against the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Gen 6 Pro. According to the tests, the Exynos 2700 performed 9.5% better than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 in Geekbench 6.5. It also performed 5% better in gaming and 24% better in gaming under low-power conditions. It’s no secret that the Exynos 2700 is coming and will power many phones in the upcoming Galaxy S27 series , at least in some regions. However, if you’re wondering whether an Exynos chipset in your next Galaxy flagship means poor gaming performance and thermal throttling, Samsung may have good news. According to a report from South Korean outlet SEDaily , citing industry sources, the Exynos 2700 outperformed the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro in an in-house evaluation by Samsung. The report further claims that the Exynos chip beat Qualcomm’s Snapdragon chip in multiple categories.

title: Sony’s Xperia 10 VIII just leaked ahead of its big reveal
summary: We're still searching for what changed.
body: TL;DR A leaked image appears to give us an early look at the Sony Xperia 10 VIII ahead of its August 25 unveiling. The phone looks remarkably similar to the Xperia 10 VII, retaining the flat back, horizontal dual-camera bar, and side-mounted fingerprint reader. Leaks also point to the same Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 and 8GB of RAM, leaving us wondering where Sony’s biggest upgrades will come from. A few days ago, we reported that Sony could unveil the Xperia 10 VIII this week. We may not have to wait until the event to see what it looks like, though. Android Headlines has now shared an image that appears to show Sony’s Xperia 10 VIII out in the wild. The image shows a woman holding the phone and looking at the screen. More importantly, we get a clear look at the back. The phone appears to have a white finish with a slight green tint, and if you’ve seen the Xperia 10 VII before, you’ll probably notice something immediately: Sony hasn’t changed much.

title: GrapheneOS’ Motorola plans include 7 years of updates, foldables, and more
summary: Graphene just can't stop talking about its Motorola plans, and we're all ears.
body: TL;DR GrapheneOS says it plans to support both regular Motorola phones as well as Razr foldables. The project says next-gen Snapdragon chips will bring the MTE and secure element improvements needed for GrapheneOS. GrapheneOS also requires a seven-year update commitment on devices. GrapheneOS has revealed a lot more about its plans to expand beyond Pixel phones to Motorola devices. The project has now confirmed that its Motorola partnership will eventually cover both traditional smartphones as well as Razr foldables. The privacy-focused Android operating system says its initial focus will be a regular, non-folding flagship, with the first supported Motorola devices expected to arrive in 2027.

title: I canceled Netflix a year ago — here’s the unexpected alternative I finally stuck with
summary: I never expected to find myself fawning over Apple TV.
body: I have been in a streaming rut for some time. I canceled my Netflix subscription last year after growing increasingly dissatisfied with the platform. However, finding a Netflix alternative that sticks, especially in a market with limited competition, has been a challenge. I cycled through a few options and couldn’t find one that really kept me hooked or made me feel like I was getting my money’s worth. And the platform I finally settled on — Apple TV — was the last one I expected to capture my loyalty.

title: Google’s foldable strategy is broken, and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold proves it
summary: This Fold left me cold.
body: Google launched the Pixel 11 series last week, and as someone with a soft spot for foldables, there was one phone I immediately wanted to learn more about: the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. I’ve spent a fair amount of time with foldables lately, especially after using Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra . So, I was genuinely curious to see how Google would respond. Would the new Pixel Fold finally feel like a good alternative? Would Google fix some of the things that held back last year’s model? title: 6 Android phones with microSD card slots you can still buy in 2026
summary: Say "no" to overpriced storage.
body: The smartphone industry is finally feeling the full effect of RAMageddon in 2026, as prices have shot up across the board due to rising memory costs. Brands are no longer able (or unwilling) to absorb the higher cost of components, so this is now passed on to us, the consumers. Smartphones with higher RAM and storage now command a steep premium, even more so than before. Thankfully, a small segment of smartphones still exists that has a solution for the storage crisis — the microSD card slot. It’s mostly entry-level and a few mid-range Android phones that still support the microSD card, but there are some good models to choose from. Flagship Android phones have largely done away with this feature, except for a few specialized models that aren’t widely available in the US.

With the new Pixel 11 series, Google’s releasing its updated Pixel Camera 11 app, including redesigned Quick access sliders. Let’s take a look at what these do, and how you’ll access them. title: I’m quitting Kindle, and Amazon’s new DRM update proves why you should too
summary: I’m finally ready to leave the Kindle world behind.
body: The Kindle Oasis was released in 2019, and it’s been a while since Amazon added a meaningful update to the system. So, when I learned that Amazon was rolling out a new system software update this past week, I was quite excited. That’s until I learned that the update closes a long-standing loophole for library books borrowed via Libby that lets you hold onto a book longer than you’d otherwise be allowed. Additionally, it further tightens DRM to ensure buyers can’t offload books from the Kindle. While the first feature doesn’t affect me much, the latter, as someone who likes preserving digital media, makes the update an instant no-go for me. On paper, these changes protect publishers’ rights and intellectual property. For the end user, though, they are just another reminder that you never truly own your digital library or even the hardware you technically bought.

title: Survey suggests this is the slowest carrier if you have a cheap phone
summary: There's good news for T-Mobile subscribers with cheap phones, though.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Verizon recorded the biggest gap in cellular speeds between flagship and budget phones, according to a new survey. T-Mobile had the smallest gap in speeds between high-end and cheap phones. The survey also showed that Verizon recorded the lowest average speed for cheap phones in general. The latest flagship Android phones are often equipped with blazing-fast cellular speeds owing to more advanced modems. But a new survey suggests that the speed gap between flagship and budget phones can also be accentuated by the carrier. A survey by Recon Analytics (h/t: PhoneArena ) yielded over 4,300 speed tests across US carriers. The survey found that flagship phones often had faster speeds than budget devices on the same network. That isn’t a surprise on its own, as high-end phones tend to get faster modems.
